land.text: the Brittonic Pennine uplands of the Yorkshire Dales

predecessors.note: No page opened gives the origin of the kingdom.

successors.note: 'The Brittonic region of northwestern England was absorbed by Anglian Northumbria in the 7th century' (Hen Ogledd page); the year 625/626 is Cliopatria's.

capitals.name: Dent (name-place; no seat is recorded)
capitals.note: No page opened names a seat. Dent, Cumbria is the town whose name 'may survive' from the kingdom, 'founded and named after King Dunot the Great of the North Pennines' (Dent page); it lies about 4 km west of the Cliopatria shape.

keyframe_review.note: 592-622, 1,515 km2 (lat 53.66-54.41, lon -2.39 to -1.89): the Yorkshire Dales, where the Hen Ogledd page puts 'Regio Dunutinga – a minor kingdom or region in North Yorkshire mentioned in the Life of Wilfrid'. No page gives an area or a boundary, so the infobox check is impossible. The shape's west edge lies about 4 km east of Dent, whose name 'may survive' from the kingdom (Dent page). Cliopatria's Wikipedia field for this row is 'Dunoding', which is the Welsh kingdom of Eifionydd and Ardudwy (Dunoding page: 'existed between the 5th and 10th centuries', 'Eifionydd and Ardudwy'), not this state; the row is a different Dunoting.
623-625, 1,515 km2, the same as 592-622; unverified: no page dates the kingdom's years, which are Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Yorkshire Dales around the head of Wensleydale, Wharfedale and Dentdale

ledger.note: 592: Cliopatria's Dunoting begins. The Hen Ogledd page calls it 'a minor kingdom or region in North Yorkshire mentioned in the Life of Wilfrid', 'named for a ruler named Dunaut, perhaps the Dunaut ap Pabo known from the genealogies'; the Dent page has a 'dark age kingdom known in Latin as Regione Dunutinga'. No opened page dates its start.

625: Dunoting is absorbed by Northumbria. The page says only that 'The Brittonic region of northwestern England was absorbed by Anglian Northumbria in the 7th century'; 625 is Cliopatria's last year (its Northumbria shape grows in 626).

certainty.note: Nothing fixes the kingdom's frontiers; the shape is Cliopatria's estimate.

notes:
Kingdom of Dunoting (2 Cliopatria shapes, 592-625), budget 1-2 pages; three opened (the Dunoding page is the wrong state, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunoting did not load: url_not_found).
CLIOPATRIA LINK IS WRONG: polities.csv gives Wikipedia 'Dunoding' and Wikidata Q2264840 for this row, but the shape is in the Yorkshire Dales, while the Wikipedia 'Dunoding' article is the Welsh sub-kingdom of Gwynedd (Eifionydd and Ardudwy, 5th-10th centuries, ruling line 'expired in c. 925'). This dossier sets wikipedia to null and keeps the Q-id as Cliopatria gives it; the Q-id probably identifies the Welsh kingdom and should be checked.
ALL YEARS ARE CLIOPATRIA'S (confidence 1): no opened page dates the kingdom. The Hen Ogledd and Dent pages give only the Latin name Regio Dunutinga, the eponym Dunaut / Dunot and a location in North Yorkshire / Dent. The Life of Wilfrid is the primary source; a gap-filler should find a page on it (or on Elmet, Craven, 'Dunaut ap Pabo').
The Welsh Dunoding (Meirionnydd) has no Cliopatria row of its own and needs a dossier if the project wants it (the Gwynedd dossier may cover it).
